steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: They say that Lake Silberneherze is most beautiful during winter.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Winter seals the lake in a case of ice, and from afar it looks for all the world like a great gemstone, revealing a most breathtaking beauty in the brilliant sunlight.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But if you were to observe from up close, perhaps you would be able to appreciate its beauty even further.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: There is no gem so flawless, yet so adamant; beneath the ice, its waters yet flow.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Since when did you decide to take up poetry?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: According to the directives of the Vine-Bead Court, we will follow behind the Saintess, walking from the ice to below the feet of the statue of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: This is hardly what I would call a short stroll, and all sorts of mishaps can befall us while we walk.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis, are you worried that the ice beneath your feet might shatter?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: How very unlike you.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: You know that's not what I'm talking about.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Many of the guests of ours who are here to 'attend' will be watching us with keen eyes.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Your plans for defensive maneuvers still lack accurate information, Enciodes. We are not in what I would call a favorable position.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Allowing that Trilby Asher to approach the statue of Kjeragandr yesterday was my mistake.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If we have need of it, I can go and settle things with him right now.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: If our quarry has already sensed aught amiss, then acting now would already be too late.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: This terrible habit of yours of neglecting the bigger picture when you take action... Forget it, you and Enciodes are pretty much the same. I'm not asking either of you to change your ways.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: All I ask is that next time, please go to the trouble of restraining yourselves, just for a little bit. You'll save me from having to wrack my brain to find ways to clean up your messes.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Duly noted, Gnosis. What do you think, Enciodes?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I have not the strength to casually cut apart a giant statue tens of meters high.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You merely invited that Doctor over, who then proceeded to nearly ruin our plans is all.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: ...*sigh*

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I have no desire to listen to the two of you jibe and snipe at each other with your nonsense.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Now, about the Tschäggättä responsible for keeping order...

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: They will be posted to the island ahead of time.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: As for who is in charge of the reception for the Victorians, there are several merchants who will take care of the matter.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Gnosis, you are far too tense.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We have already completed all the preparations we can do. All we can do now is wait.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And wait we shall.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Spring is just around the corner.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I still remember when the Saintess descended from atop Mount Karlan three years ago.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: That day, Kjeragandr sent us Her blessings, and even that Enciodes couldn't help but kneel... I do not know if we will ever see such miracles again these days.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Seems like seeing the sights of today has hooked up your old memories, my friend.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: But Arctosz, don't you think you've been wallowing in those memories too often these past few years?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Rather than putting your efforts into sarcasm, Ratatos, you should care more about today's ceremony.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I've felt that something was off ever since I woke up this morning... Don't you think Kjeragandr's statue looks a little bit different compared to yesterday?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: You Browntails were in charge of managing construction, so you'd better think up a real good explanation for the Saintess!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Heh, no need to worry about that...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Hey, Arctosz, why's your face look like that?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Did that Trilby Asher rough you up or something?

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Well, it's like you said! No need to worry about that!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: (The girl's real feisty, just like Tatyana. Just like me.)

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: (Not bad.)

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Patriarch, Matriarch, everyone is present.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Good. Let the people below know that they can head to their designated positions and wait for now.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: The Saintess will arrive soon. If anyone dares to tarnish the Browntail name at this critical moment, I won't be showing any mercy!

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Understood, Matriarch.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Wait a moment, Yucatan.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Why's it just you? Where's your wife?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: It's almost time already, why's she not here?

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Rus told me this morning that she had a few things to do...

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: She wants to prepare a pleasant surprise for you, Matriarch.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I'm not sure if I should look forward to a pleasant surprise from her.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: What could possibly be more important than today's ceremony? Can't she pick a better time to give me a headache?!

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: I... I'll send her a message right away.

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Don't worry, Matriarch. Rus is very clear on what she should be prioritizing.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I should have figured that you'd be on your wife's side.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Alright, alright. She's no longer a girl. Guess I'll just have to wait and see what this 'pleasant surprise' of hers is.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Anyway, if she's off doing things, why didn't she bring you along?

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: Rus already has someone helping her out...

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: Everyone, the time has come.

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: The Saintess arrives.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Please, lend me your ears.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It has been three years since the Vine-Bead Court has recognized those foreigners who wish to devote themselves to Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjerag today is capable of incredible growth and development, but that growth rests on the shoulders of the good folk here today, alongside the toil and devotion of all Kjerag's people.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I believe that you all have seen the change that has come to Kjerag these past few years with your own eyes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjeragandr has given Her people, Her children, a challenge, and we have already given Her our answer.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Yet these past three years are merely the beginning.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: In the coming days, we will meet with more complex situations than ever before, and Kjerag will see its fair share of trials and tribulations.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: However, I hope that we all believe that Kjeragandr will not abandon this land of Kjerag, and neither will She abandon the lives of those who live upon it, for She so loves Her people.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: This great statue of Kjeragandr will be the main symbol of Kjerag to the outside world.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: At the same time, it will become a vessel for all the love that Her faithful show to Her.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Hereafter, one need not climb Mount Karlan to make one's devotions to Her. You need but face towards Her during your prayers.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It is my wish that the faith you have in Her is not constrained by the trappings of ceremony.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I believe that true faith has taken root in the hearts of all of Kjerag's people.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Now, I ask of you to walk with me, walk with me under the gaze of Kjeragandr towards the foot of Her holy statue, where we will pray for Her to bestow Her blessings upon Kjerag!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: By Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: By Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: By Kjeragandr!
The many voices by the lake that cry out Kjeragandr's name blend and merge together.
The Saintess stands at the head of the crowd, and takes the first step onto the ice.
The frozen Lake Silberneherze shines like a flawless gem when looked upon from afar.
But only once you stand atop it will you see that this 'gem' is covered in chips and cracks.

The ice is covered in cracks wending and weaving across the surface, the endlessly churning waters beneath the ice surging about together. Under the dawn light, it is as if the soul of the lake itself was wandering about in an eternal cycle.
In the eyes of the people of Kjerag, such a sight was so beautiful as to be breathtaking.

Kjeragandr's Saintess steps across the cracks that seemed like they were carved by the biting winds, as if walking past a millennium's worth of Kjerag's bitterly cold hardships, as if walking past its endless winter days.
Because now, spring was just around the corner.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: How the hell are they not here yet?!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Are you kidding me?!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: The communicator doesn't work. Didn't they say they'd be getting to Kjerag last night, so they'd definitely catch the train today?!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Huff... hah...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Calm down, Sciurus... Calm down.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Okay... I've calmed down. The Saintess needs to walk across the ice to the island, so the ceremony won't be starting quite so soon. I've still got time.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Think about the look on Ratatos's face when this is all over...)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Aha, hahaha!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: *cough* *cough* Ahem.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (I've definitely got the time right, and punctuality is par for the course on that side.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (A little lateness is one thing. We won't be too late now, I'm sure.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (I think the train to Lake Silberneherze should be pulling into the station right around now.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Alright, let me see, the next train is arriving at...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Why's it so late?!

steps.name: Station Steward
steps.text: Madam Sciurus, that train is a local that stops at every station. It's natural that it's somewhat delayed...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I don't care if it's natural, I need that train here right now!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Damn it all, I can't just sit here and wait!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Get me in touch with the station master! I want that train sped up right away!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: If it doesn't need to stop, then it better not stop! Make sure it's going at full speed too!

steps.name: Station Steward
steps.text: But, Madam!

steps.name: Station Steward
steps.text: If we do that, it would greatly inconvenience the passengers aboard the train!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: As long as they end up where they wanted to go, it should be fine, right?

steps.name: Station Steward
steps.text: Eh? Ah, well, yes, but...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: No buts!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Monch! MONCH!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Here, Madam.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Get in touch with the manager of 'BangBang Burdenbeast' for me! Get them to round up every single one of their free burdenbeasts right now!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Anyone waiting to get on the train at the stations that it passes, get them a burdenbeast to take them wherever they want!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Yes, Madam.

steps.name: Station Steward
steps.text: Madam Sciurus, is... is this really alright?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: You got a problem with it?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Right, thanks for reminding me.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: We'll need to prepare a small gift for everyone already aboard the train. We'll call it a token of apology for disrupting their journey. Use the souvenirs that you sell on the trains for that!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: All expenses can go to Clan Browntail... No, wait, put it all on my personal account!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Understood. It shall be done.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I hope that's enough... No, it's definitely enough!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: For sure...!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Faster!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Don't forget what we're here to do! In the back, keep pace!

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Halt! Gather up!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Form up!

steps.name: Stern Soldier
steps.text: Sir! Reporting in! Second Squad in formation, sir!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Very good then.

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: And Third Squad?

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Sir! Reporting in! Third Squad in formation, sir!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Very good.

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Jack, have your squad bring up the rear!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: I want constant vigilance! Don't overlook a single enemy!

steps.name: Slippery Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: Good, keep those spirits up!

steps.name: Lead Soldier
steps.text: All squads, forward march!

steps.name: Victorian Soldiers
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: What are those Victorians up to now? Are they holding... weapons?

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: Surely not? Aren't they here to attend the ceremony or something?

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: Have you ever seen them line up in formation like that before? It... It must be all just for show...

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: I've gotta say, I don't think they've got the same look to them as they did before.

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: By Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: Kjeragandr protect us from harm...

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Reporting in, sir!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: We've finished scouting ahead. The Saintess has already started leading everyone over to the island!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Are our men all prepared?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: All troops in formation! Ready to commence operations at any time!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Good. Keep them lined up, and await my orders.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Lake Silberneherze on a winter's day. Truly one of Kjerag's most beautiful sights.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Who would have thought that the next time I clapped eyes on this wonder would be under circumstances like this?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: You've become much gloomier these days, Harold.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Have I? Haha, you know as they say, 'soft days make soft men'.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Lisburn, after a whole month of R&R, you're still able to swing your sword around?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: It's much heavier than I remember.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: How about you, Charles?

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: It's a battlefield. We're Victorian soldiers.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Not much else I can do.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You're right. In the decades since I joined the army, never have I met finer soldiers than you all.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Am I right, Charles?

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: I think I'm gonna puke.

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: But what else can I do?

steps.name: Somber Soldier
steps.text: Give the order already, Harold.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Forgive me, my friends.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Alright, orders incoming!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Everyone, forward march!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Under the guise of building a statue of their goddess, the Kjerags have been secretly transporting military goods under our noses. We will let them know the price of trying to make a fool of Victoria!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Mission objective: destroy the statue of Kjeragandr atop the island!

steps.name: Victorian Soldiers
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: The train won't be making further stops? Are you certain of this?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Okay. Understood.

steps.name: Skeptical Passenger
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Skeptical Passenger
steps.text: Why didn't we stop at that station just now?

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: I am truly, incredibly sorry!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Ladies and gentlemen! Our train has run into a small operational issue!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Until we arrive at the station at Lake Silberneherze, the train will be increasing in speed, and will not be stopping at intervening stations...

steps.name: Astonished Passenger
steps.text: Not stopping? This is unacceptable! I'm meant to get off for sightseeing at the next station!

steps.name: Unhappy Passenger
steps.text: Me too!

steps.name: Unhappy Passenger
steps.text: I was going to go and visit the local markets too... Whyever can't you stop the train anyway?!

spans.text: I was going to go and visit the local markets too... Whyever

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: We offer our deepest apologies for this inconvenience to everyone!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: As compensation, we have prepared for all our passengers a gift as a token of our apology!

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: All passengers may freely pick a souvenir of your choice from our store aboard this train! Whether it's specialty cheeses or a burdenbeast blind box, it's all FREE OF CHARGE!!

steps.name: Astonished Passenger
steps.text: Oh... Well, if there's compensation, I suppose that's alright.

steps.name: Conductor
steps.text: Ah, that's right! I ask all passengers to note that there is a limited amount of gift-wrapped mountain ice water, so if you would like some, please come as soon as possible—

steps.name: Skeptical Passenger
steps.text: Alright, alright! No need to go on any more than that!

steps.name: Skeptical Passenger
steps.text: Okay, sure, speed up the train, no stopping at the stations, whatever! Just gimme one of those super-expensive limited-edition waters already!

steps.name: Unhappy Passenger
steps.text: Hey, no cutting in line!

steps.name: Unhappy Passenger
steps.text: Give me a water too!

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Things sure are lively today.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: What could possibly be so urgent as to rush this train to Lake Silberneherze? Is it to deliver some mystery goods, or perhaps people...?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Either way...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: I believe I win this hand.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: The trains here have all been handled, Madam.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: As per your orders, the premier train next arriving at Lake Silberneherze is now running at top speed.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: But are you sure that the guests you invited are aboard that train?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Of course I'm sure!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: It's just that, if we happened to be wrong...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: No way! They're definitely on that train!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Monch, I must ask, do you know how many new relay stations we've built to ensure a smooth signal across all of Kjerag these past three years?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I... I'm afraid I'm not quite sure.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Well, you've just returned to Kjerag, so I suppose it's natural for you not to know. So listen up and remember this!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: In Browntail territory alone, we've built five of those top-of-the-line relay stations to ensure that the signal never breaks!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: That many...?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Yep!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: We also called in some professionals courtesy of that Doctor from Rhodes Island to help out, just to make sure that even amongst our many mountains, our communications will never be blocked!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: So what I'm trying to say is that, theoretically, as long as it's within Kjerag's borders, there shouldn't be any sort of communications mishap.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Aside from some... special places.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Special places...?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Hehe, can't figure it out? They're—

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Could it possibly be the private rooms on the train, Madam?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Oh no, I shouldn't have said that...)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Heh... Bullseye!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: It's the private rooms on the train! More specifically, the private rooms on the premier train from the foot of Mount Karlan to Lake Silberneherze!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: That train was a special order from Victoria. As for the other trains that we have, they used that train as a prototype to copy- I mean, to study how to manufacture our own.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: The walls of the private rooms of that original train are inlaid with materials designed to isolate the occupants from disturbances from outside, so naturally, they will cut off communication signals too.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: The other trains don't have this feature, because, er, because it would have drastically inflated construction costs...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I get it now!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: So what you're saying is, in determining if our guests are in Kjerag already, the very fact that your communicator can't reach them tells us that they must be in that specific train's private rooms!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: That's amazing, Madam! I'm learning so much about the trains as well!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: *cough* *cough* Anyways!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Kjerag as it is now and Kjerag as of a few years ago couldn't be more different.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I'm not going to ask where you've been these past few years, Monch, and I don't intend to pry into what you've been up to then. I don't even really care about why you didn't go back to that Gnosis either.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: But if you really want to be my assistant, then you'd better get used to the modern-day Kjerag already!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: And you'd better not think that I'm still the same old Rus from three years ago, you hear me?

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Yes, Madam!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I'll do my best!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Glad to hear it!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Eh? Why's there so many people outside?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Hey, wait, aren't they...?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Get back! I said get back!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: All of you, not a step closer!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: You... What the hell do you think you're doing?!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: How dare you try and pull this stunt under Kjeragandr's gaze! Don't even think about trying to ruin today's ceremony!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: Jack?

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: That's you, isn't it, Jack? What are you playing at?!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: You... You've just had a bit too much to drink, right?

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: A word of advice from me, today's not the time to make a ruckus! Go tell the others quick, Jack—

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Enough!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: I am under orders to shoot dead the next person who steps forward!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Woman
steps.text: Eek!

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: You know, back when you first showed up, people said that a bunch of foreign soldiers showing up in Kjerag couldn't be up to any good.

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: I didn't believe them. I even spoke up for you guys.

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: It seems that I was blind this entire time. So, this was your real purpose? To ruin our ceremony for Kjeragandr? To strike us down?

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: Kjeragandr will not forgive you for this.

steps.name: Common Kjerag Man
steps.text: You invite Her wrath upon yourselves!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Hah. Let Her try.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: We were punished enough as it is, a long time ago.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Those are Victorian soldiers. Something's not right. They have their uniforms on, and they've got their weapons out too!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: It looks like there's been some sort of commotion outside!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Please, hide yourself, Madam...
The black-haired girl is about to subconsciously hold out her arm to protect her employer.
But before the words can even leave her mouth, Sciurus proves to be a step ahead of her, covering her mouth with her own hand and pulling her into a corner.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Shh!)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Don't say a word, Monch. We need to stay hidden!)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Those Victorians... Didn't they say they were just here to attend the ceremony? Hmph. I guess they've finally shown their true colors.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (This operation of theirs seems pretty big.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (That bitch Ratatos wouldn't know about this trouble yet, would she?)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Madam, they have a whole squad of Tschäggättä stationed there, alongside Degenbrecher from Karlan Trade. If trouble reaches them, it probably won't last very long.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Yeah... You're probably right.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (And with Yucatan there, my sister will be safe.)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Madam, allow me to escort you somewhere safe. I'll go assist Sir Yucatan next.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (No. I have to stay here to watch them. If things get even more heated here, at least I can stop them for a bit.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Look, don't worry, nothing's going to happen to me. Even if I did get found, considering that I'm an envoy between Kjerag and Victoria for multiple cooperative business ventures, I doubt they'll have the stones to mess with me.)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Madam...)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Don't look at me like that! I already told you, I'm not the same as I was three years ago!)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Okay, listen up, Monch. I've got something I need you to do.)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Yes, Madam! You need only say the word!)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (That Enciodes definitely has some sort of contingency plan up his sleeve for those Victorians. Considering how big this commotion's grown, I can only suspect that something's gone wrong with the deployment of his men.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Monch, I need you to investigate things for me. Go check up on what's happening over there, and if you get the chance, making the Silverashes owe the Browntails a favor would be pretty nice.)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Understood. I'll get it done.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (What? Something on my face?)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Madam...)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (You really have grown.)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Wh-Who asked you?!)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (You're a lot younger than me, you know! Stop acting like you're the big sister! Really, you should be treating me like the big sister!)

spans.text: (You're a lot younger than me, you know! Stop acting like you're the big sister! Really,

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Can I really call you sister?)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (*cough* *cough* We... We'll discuss this later!)

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: (Alright, get moving already!)

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: (Yes, Madam!)
From time to time, Degenbrecher thinks back to ten years ago.
Back then, every winter she would accompany Enciodes all across Kjerag.
That young man who had just returned to his home country was not yet the deeply experienced person he was now, still quite underripe. He had to do many things himself, rushing about to and fro.
One could say that he was hot-blooded, or one could say that he had ambition.
Degenbrecher remembered that in the winter of that year, Enciodes brought all his plans and stratagems that he had devised in Victoria back to Kjerag, where he single-handedly founded Karlan Trade.
Of the few people who could be called his confidants, she would have just barely been within their number.
And thus, she found herself staying in this cold, snowy land.
If you were to ask her, while she has long gotten used to the bitter chill, she does not actually like cold weather very much.
Kazimierz's winters were cold indeed.
Those days, she would make her way through many matches of the Majors in winter. This made the KGCC very unhappy, but whether or not her opponent was happy was never in her mind.
Going back even further, Leithanien's winters too, were cold.
Was Kjerag's winter not colder than Kazimierz's or Leithanien's?
Degenbrecher stamped her foot upon the ice's surface, frost crystals breaking loose under her step.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Thinking back to old times?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I remember that year when we had just arrived back in Kjerag from Victoria, we had crossed Lake Silberneherze as well.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But back then, it was because all the roads had been snowed out.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: With no railroads or mechanized shovels or vehicles specially designed to handle snow, we were barely able to maintain a handful of flat main streets.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Under such heavy snowfalls, and with Karlan Trade only barely having started up, goods piled up behind snowbanks blocking the road, and the trade routes stagnated. We were on the brink of coming to a complete stop...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In the end, it was you who helped Leones gather up his burdenbeasts, and by using them to carry those goods across Lake Silberneherze, we were able to alleviate that particular crisis.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You talk too much, Enciodes.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I assumed that you would have shown more solemnity in light of the ceremony, not take it as an opportunity to babble about old happenings.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: My apologies.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Some things are simply too unexpected in the moment, and so it is hard not to constantly bring them back to the forefront of one's mind, especially during interesting times such as these.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Who would have expected the great Black Knight to be so proficient at riding a burdenbeast.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you are curious as to why I know how to ride a burdenbeast, then you need only ask.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I learnt it when I was young.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In Leithanien?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: In Leithanien.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If there is ever the opportunity, I could bring the both of you to do some sightseeing.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's not a very exciting place, so don't expect too much.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: How is it, compared to Kjerag?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It's not as good.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Kjerag is nowhere near as cold.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This is the first time I've ever heard you give such an idealistic assessment.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: That's enough out of you.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Alright. We've arrived.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Everyone, please come forward.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: With Kjeragandr as our witness, this ceremony shall soon begin.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Let us pray—

steps.name: Kjarr
steps.text: ...It appears that some of our more excitable guests can't wait for their cue.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Just who is causing that clamor there?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: (Gah, I didn't need this pain in my ass right now!)

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Yucatan! Why the hell isn't your wife here yet?!

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: I just got in contact with her, and she says she's nearly here...!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: What do you mean 'nearly here'?!

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Listen, you get back in touch with her right now, tell her to go to the moons or something, as far away as possible, just don't come over!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: What is going on over here?! What's all this commotion about?!

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: Sir! Those Victorians don't look as friendly as they usually do!

steps.name: Gulo
steps.text: I saw that they've got some pretty big weapons of some kind, and they looked real enough to me!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: I knew that they were going stab us in the back!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: Let them come! It's a good thing I told the Paleroche boys to prepare for this! We meet them in battle!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Hold, Sir Arctosz!

steps.name: Arctosz
steps.text: But... Saintess!

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Saintess! Sir Enciodes!

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: The Victorian troops have broken through our guards who were maintaining order, they draw near!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Send out several squads, and prioritize the safety of any commoners about!

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Yes, Saintess!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: They have made their move. It appears they have several squads of their own lined up to approach us.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And at their head is that viscount.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: What's the plan?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Where are Weiss and Matterhorn?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: We haven't received any news from them since last night.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: They should have been watching the movements of the Victorian Army very closely, and an operation of this size would have prompted a report by now.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Unless they had no way of sending that report.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Beware Victorians, even as they bear gifts.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Despite my belief that I had managed to establish a strong enough relationship with Viscount Craigavon, it appears that we have not been able to move his heart from its course.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: This is no time to stand around licking your wounds, Enciodes.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: They're already far past the point of pretending to be friendly with us.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: They are professional Victorian troops. Whether using drone arrays to bombard us, or hiding their casters in the crowd, their ruthless efficacy is clear.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This is still what they consider 'pressure'. They have not begin to use 'force' just yet.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: And I assume you have some sort of plan for this?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We cannot allow them to disrupt the ceremony.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Not only will the Vine-Bead Court and the three clans suffer a drastic blow to their reputations, they will lose the trust of the people of Kjerag, alongside the respect of those outside its borders... We would be caught in truly dire straits.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Not exactly the easiest task.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: You sound concerned, Enciodes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: We must not allow a true war with Victoria to begin. We need only wait until the next perso... the next distinguished guest arrives.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But at the very least, we cannot allow them to get any closer to the statue of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: But they're pretty much here already.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'll go stop them.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Now's not a good time for jokes.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: They've got at least two thousand troops out there, how exactly are you going to fight them alone?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: It will be easier than me having to handle you after a night out, Gnosis.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Like I said, this really isn't a good time to joke around!

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Who do you think, out of the many people that he knows, Enciodes always calls first?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: ...*sigh* You're going to get yourself killed.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you don't want me to be killed, then you should put in some more work, Gnosis.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Degenbrecher, I'm sure you're already aware of the risks at hand.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I need you to hold them back, at least until we have settled our arrangements here.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: At this time, Karlan Trade, no, 'Kjerag' cannot assist you in the slightest. This is to be the sole work of the Black Knight.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Are you able to do it?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Heh. This wouldn't be the first time.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You all wait here.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It's not good to hold your anger in, Gnosis.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: The two of you have talked it over already. I'm not one to make a fuss.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: At least while Degenbrecher holds back those Victorians, I can send out men to find Weiss and Matterhorn, as well as our 'distinguished guests'.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: If they arrive a bit sooner than expected, things might just start looking up for us.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I'll leave that to you then.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: News of what is happening here will spread fast. I should be bracing myself right about now, so that I can deal with these beasts who saw fit to bare their fangs.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Hark, they come.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Halt! Everyone, gather up!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Get back into formation!

steps.name: Victorian Soldiers
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: This fog's mighty thick.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Strange, have the Tschäggättä not made their move yet? Why are they just watching from all around the sides?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Sure, our operation might have caught them with their pants down, but surely they're going to put up some resistance, right?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Don't be so quick to dismiss them. The head of the Silverash clan's one wily fellow.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh* Kjerag can't afford to go to war with Victoria, but us? We can pretty much take a crap atop their holiest of holies. It's a real funny thing, diplomacy.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: The way things are now, I don't think they've got any room to play defense at the moment.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Well, you won't know until you give them a poke.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Let some other men advance for now! If the Saintess and Clan Silverash still don't react, then we continue with our original plan and prepare to bombard the statue of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Understood.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Wait, it looks like there's movement on their side!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: No, that can't be...

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: They've only got... one person over there?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It's her. The Black Knight. Of course. It could only be her.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Although I had guessed that this sort of thing might happen...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Seeing the real deal with your own eyes, it's enough to make a man's heart drum with excitement.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A lone woman holding back a thousand soldiers. Wow. This really is right out of one of those knight novels.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: You're joking.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: There's no one person who's got the strength to resist a whole army. The Zhayedans can't, the Silverlance Pegasi can't, not even one of the devils' Royal Courts could.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: We've seen this sort of thing before ourselves, Harold.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I know. Of course I do. 'You might kill us, but you won't kill any more.'

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But do we really have to pay this price to get what we want?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Our army is a machine, consuming an unending amount of fresh meat just so that it can lurch forward once more. Right now, hah, there's just us old boys left.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: We can't bear the cost of it much longer.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You know me, Lisburn.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I've always been a bit of a miser.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And a miser's heart weeps at every coin lost. As long as they keep bubbling up to the top of my mind, I can hardly sleep soundly at night.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: We're soldiers. We've got no choice.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You're right. It's all for Victoria.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Send the order down, all men, prepare for war!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'll take the lead, and I'll bring along my top brass to meet the legendary Black Knight face to face!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: Hey, Harold, I'm not going to stop you now.

steps.name: Seasoned Soldier
steps.text: But I've got to ask, how's it feel having to face down the Black Knight that you like so much in the ring?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Not great.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Reminds me of one time during my youth, when I was getting teased at one of the Duke's parties. I ended up drinking an entire cup's worth of straight shots at once.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: A lot of bitterness, a lot of burning, and a lot of retching.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Enough to make you faint, but I will say that I also feel a bit of... excitement.
Harold Craigavon looked towards Kjerag's endless snowscape.
All about him, frost blanketed the icy surface of Lake Silberneherze, mist gathered in the air, and in the distance, the statue of Kjeragandr loomed, Her face fuzzy and indistinct.

The chill extending all about Her feet made people feel as though they had truly entered the realm of a snow god. The frozen surface of the lake looked as though it was a great shard of rock sugar, covered in icing.
In this unreal, dreamlike environment, these men wearing their valor on their sleeve stood out like a sore thumb, and across from them—
A vague silhouette appeared within the dense fog that laid thick in the air.
Their adversary walked forward, step by step, treading atop the ice and snow towards them. It felt like with every step, she commanded the strength to stop a thousand men in their tracks.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This is as far as you go.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And you will go no further.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: If you wish to watch the ceremony, you may watch from here alongside me.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I would be truly honored to have you accompany me, Madam Degenbrecher!

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: By all rights, I should accept your kind offer, but...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: As a most trusted partner, Her Grace is very concerned about Kjerag's development issues, and has given me orders to approach the base of Kjeragandr, so as to show our good faith.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Concern?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Concern armed to the teeth and carrying cannons is a very rare sight indeed.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Force of circumstance, I do hope you understand.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Lately, there has been a most unlawful force at play, wantonly moving prohibited materials about Kjerag under the guise of constructing the statue of Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: According to our intelligence, the stronghold of this force happens to be exactly under this holy statue of yours.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: And so, Her Grace was so concerned about this issue that she commissioned me and my men overnight to investigate.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: A likely story.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: It is, in the end, Her Grace's intent.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Who could say if there truly is such a dangerous power underneath the feet of Kjeragandr's statue?

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But if the Great Saintess and Sir Enciodes were to meet with unfortunate accidents, it would be far too late for regrets by then.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Nobody would like to see something like that happen, am I right, Madam Degenbrecher?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I don't really care what you say.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: And naturally, what we do here is none of your business.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: The people of Kjerag will handle their own issues. We don't need outsiders to order us about.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: I'm afraid that's that, then. I'm truly sorry it came to this, but this is where I must carry out my duty.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Also, please excuse my curiosity, Madam Degenbrecher, but considering you managed to hold your tongue so well while I jabbered on...

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: You don't plan on causing delay for us, do you?

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You talk far too much.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: Haha, well, when you're at my age, it's hard not to be a bit of a windbag.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: But as for you, Madam Degenbrecher.

steps.name: Harold
steps.text: As I've now learnt, you're not the sort of person to indulge in mindless chatter.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: That's why I hate overly-chatty smartasses.
The woman says no more, slowly unsheathing her long swordbreaker from about her waist.
The scraping of the metal lets out a ear-piercing shriek, ending with the sound of it burying its point into the ice, a sound that induces a trembling in the men that none are able to stymie.
Since they got the intended message, there is not much more need for words.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: This manner is more to my tastes.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I'll say it again.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: You will go no further.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: —None may enter.
